reviews.comment: While he was a nice guy and you can tell he likes teaching this subject but there was a LOT of reading for every class time. We had to have read parts of the many books we had to get and articles to be prepared for class. While the reading wasn't difficult if folklore isn't your speed, you probably won't like this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Harris was awesome. I took him for 358. I had zero interest in screenwriting going into his class, and still don't, but Professor Harris made writing so enjoyable. There is absolutely no way you do poorly in this class if you attend, but the experience is great too. Plus you get to watch parts of some great movies.

He was very understanding, and a nice guy. You could take some classes on Zoom. It's a lot of writing, and things are due at weird times so be sure to keep an eye on it, but as long as you submit everything you're going to get an A.

(This was for ENGL 391 it just didnt let me chose it) Prof Harris is a very generous, caring and friendly guy. While attendance was mandatory, he always understood if you were late or absent. There was a lot of reading required from textbooks that you must buy. Grades lenient but due dates for the assignments are often weird.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: I really, really loved Dr. Harris! His class was extremely easy and fun. He does assign a lot of reading and books (which you need to purchase). But honestly, I never did any of it and I ended up fine. His feedback is always very helpful and easy to understand. If you're looking for an easy, yet fun, A, take this class!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is a very nice man and the course is a guaranteed A if you do all the work. However, it is a lot of work. It's not hard, but it is time consuming. The peer reviews are just so boring. Also, he is a rambler and mumbles (SO MUCH!!), so a lot of times class is hard to get through. However, if you want a nice GPA booster, it's a good choice.

Creative writing is already a fun course, and I really liked Harris with it. He gave great feedback on the pieces and I enjoyed writing for it. The peer reviews are a lot of writing, but it really is an hour a week for like, three weeks out of the semester. Not hard. Altogether just put basic effort into it and have some fun.

His CW class is well structured but he does require a lot of reading. I never did any of the reading and did fine. Dr. Harris is very kind and flexible, which made the class worth it for me. IMO the class is a little too fast paced to fit all the genres, but its manageable. I would have just liked more time to draft so i could put out better work.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He can take up the first ten minutes of class just taking about nothing and then let you out late. This is the prose workshop class. Its a lot of reading which is to be expected but also a lot of outside sources (not just peers to workshop). There are 10 short answer questions on each peer review which takes way longer than it should.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved taking his class. I especially liked writing papers in this course because, he would give clear instructions and good feedback. My only complaint would be that I had trouble hearing him during class lectures and discussions because he would walk around the room with his nose in a book .
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He isn't a bad professor, but he assigns a lot of reading and we had a quiz over the assigned reading at the beginning of class. You cannot fall behind in the reading because it is hard to catch up. The exams consisted of few multiple choice, some true/false, and a lot of open-ended questions and an essay.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES
Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He was fine. He wasn't great and he wasn't terrible. He took a bit of time to get used to, since he's a little weird, but once the semester got going I didn't mind him as much. This is just a really hard class and he tries his best to make it easier, but there's not getting around the amount of work you have to do. It's a writing class for a reason
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Decent prof. Assigned a fairly heavy workload. He assigned 2 papers, a group project, 2 exams (midterm and final), weekly discussion posts, and of course, concurrent reading.  I am a fairly fast reader and I really struggled to keep up with the readings because they were long. Sometimes up to 100 pages a night.  Class discussions were interesting.

This class may not be easy for everyone, but Professor Harris is really willing to help. As long as you utilize his feedback and go to him with any questions, you should be fine. There were three 6-8 page papers and one 10-14 page paper, along with pop quizzes and peer review participation grades. Read all assigned materials and you'll be fine.
He's a good prof. As long as you go to class and do the readings, you'll be fine. He's really helpful in office hours too. He gives great feedback and gives suggestions on what to add to your papers.

Easy class - comp & rhetoric. Had assigned readings, read the first week, never opened books again. Easy grader. 4 tests a semester, "final" is the research paper at the end. Even let us re-edit a previous paper for a better grade. Only disadvantage is that he's quiet and mumbles. Attendance is counted in participation grade. Definitely take him.
